findings.title: Async create replays the original object instead of the unified result
findings.body: The legacy write uses the original `obj`, not the object returned by `Storage.Create`. Storage commonly assigns server-generated metadata such as UID, resource version, timestamps, or a generated name to its returned object. In mode 3 those values are therefore absent from the asynchronously created legacy object, leaving the two stores inconsistent and potentially making later updates/deletes target different identities.

findings.title: Async update does not apply the committed unified object to legacy
findings.body: The mode-3 update forwards the caller's `objInfo` directly to legacy instead of ensuring legacy receives the result committed by `Storage.Update`. The unified storage may normalize the object or assign metadata, and `objInfo.UpdatedObject` may also be stateful or produce a different result on a second invocation. Consequently the legacy copy can diverge from the successful unified update, defeating the safety-copy purpose of this mode.

findings.title: Delete loses the request logger in the context
findings.body: This constructs the logging context with `d.Log` rather than the per-request `log` that includes the object name, kind, and method. The delete calls (including the asynchronous legacy delete) therefore lack those request-scoped fields, making failures difficult to correlate; it also drops any logger already attached to the incoming context.

findings.title: Update storage failures are recorded as legacy failures
findings.body: When `Storage.Update` returns an error, this records the duration through `recordLegacyDuration` even though no legacy operation ran. The storage failure is thus attributed to the legacy backend in dual-writer metrics, producing incorrect reliability and latency signals for operators.

findings.title: Delete-collection legacy metrics are recorded as storage metrics
findings.body: The asynchronous legacy delete-collection result is reported via `recordStorageDuration`. Failures and latency of the legacy operation are therefore counted against storage, while legacy metrics remain falsely successful or absent, obscuring the very fallback-write failures mode 3 is intended to monitor.

findings.title: Delete duration metric uses the name as the kind label
findings.body: On successful unified deletes this passes `name` to `recordStorageDuration` where the corresponding error path and other methods pass `options.Kind`. Per-object names will be emitted as the kind label, breaking metric consistency and potentially creating high-cardinality time series.
